tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0

**Edition: v0 — November 5, 2026. Status: validated and frozen.**

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.
## 35. Transfer and Pinning

Value transfer is prohibited when it would invalidate an active derived access. A legal transfer does not turn a second-class authority into a freely copyable persistent reference and must preserve its validity chain and anchor dependencies.

Transferring a value never physically moves storage owned by it. Moving an **in-place** leaf is rejected when that leaf is pinned; pinning only the owned storage does not prohibit transfer of the owning value. Detailed constraints belong to `transfer` (O4), `Pinned`, and pinning invariant I5.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract
## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

## 9. Abstract Allocations and Admissible State

An abstract allocation has at least:

- a **unique identity** within the abstract execution;
- an **address space**;
- a **base address**;
- an **extent** expressed in bytes;
- a strictly positive, power-of-two **alignment** satisfied by its base;
- a **live** or **dead** state;
- abstract offset-indexable storage made up of abstract bytes;
- if deallocatable, **deallocation-authority** conditions.

An abstract allocation does not necessarily correspond to a library allocator call. The kernel also represents storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later.

**Disjointness of live allocations:** Two distinct live abstract allocations in the **same address space** occupy **disjoint** address ranges. Ranges are half-open: `[base, base + size)`. Two disjoint ranges have an empty intersection. Thus, a zero-sized range overlaps no other range.

**Allocation alignment:** Every **registered** abstract allocation, live or dead, has a strictly positive power-of-two alignment; its base is a multiple of that alignment. Valid alignment is a property of admissible states, not merely a creation-time check.

Subplaces returned by an arena or a data stack within an allocation are **not automatically new abstract allocations**: they may share its identity and provenance. The abstract machine is *flat*: it introduces no parent–child hierarchy of allocations.

The base and extent are modeled over natural numbers in this kernel. Constraints on address width, actually available spaces, and possible overflow of hardware representations are reserved for conversion, layout, and ABI rules; they are not implicitly proved by this mathematical abstraction.

**Admissible state and domain:** The abstract state contains registered allocations and a freshness discipline. **Freshness requires that a newly assigned identity has never been assigned before**, even to an allocation that has since died. A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation, not a language requirement.

Admissible states jointly satisfy:

- **Well-formedness of identities and freshness:** the preceding discipline is consistent with the registered allocations;
- **Disjointness of live allocations:** two distinct live allocations in the same address space do not overlap;
- **Alignment:** every registered allocation, live or dead, has valid alignment and an aligned base.

Normative memory semantics applies to **admissible states**, namely those satisfying these three properties. An empty state is an admissible initial state and allows reachability proofs; it is **not the only admissible initial state**. An initial configuration supplied by the environment or interoperability may be admissible if it satisfies the required invariants. Establishing such conformity belongs to the applicable initialization or interoperability contract.

**Fundamental distinction:** Well-formedness, disjointness, and alignment, as invariants of admissible states, determine the **domain** of the semantics. Their violation in an arbitrary state outside that domain **is not, by itself, a new operational obligation whose violation would be classified as UB**. Relations in a Lean model may nevertheless be mathematically total on such states; their outcomes do not bind the language specification outside the admissible domain.

**Raw creation:** In an admissible state, creation of a live allocation requires a fresh identity, valid alignment, a correctly aligned base, and no overlap with any distinct live allocation in the same space. These conditions are **operation** preconditions; their violation by an unsafe raw operation constitutes UB. They are distinct from domain invariants even when one guarantees some of them. Actual resource reservation may additionally fail in a defined manner according to the allocator contract; that case is not equated with a violation of a raw-operation precondition.

The abstract machine does not mandate a physical allocation table, `next` counter, or liveness flags at runtime; these are semantic and formalization tools.

## 10. Bytes and Initialization
# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants.

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded). Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.
## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations

1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation.
3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.

# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior

The fragments below are **traces of abstract operations**, not language syntax. The judgments illustrate normative rules; they create no exception to the detailed preconditions.

## 83. Address Reuse and Old Provenance

An allocation `a` is created and an access retains its provenance; after deallocation, a new allocation `b` may occupy the same address. `a ≠ b` as abstract identities: reading through the old access is invalid even if the addresses are equal. A new valid access with provenance `b` may be used within its rights.

## 84. Partial Initialization and Reading

A valid write to a subrange initializes its corresponding bytes. Reading another subrange that remains uninitialized is not permitted. The correspondence for logical state `Init` must guarantee a representation valid for the expected type; the mere presence of bits does not authorize type confusion.

## 85. Splitting a Structure or SoA Columns

Starting from a `Modify` authority exercised over a structure, `split` may provide `Modify` authorities over disjoint leaf regions. Modification of each region is permitted as long as the other validity and holder conditions hold; a second independent derivation over the same leaf does not become legal merely by having a distinct name.

## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical value without the required initialization.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

139	## 4. Spec problems (with evidence)
140	
141	**P0. Spec v0 does not specify either contract.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Annex D calls itself "non normative" and says "les résultats … concernent le modèle exploratoire …, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées". DS-v1 exists only in the brief. Every HandlePool/DataStack definition beyond §36/§37/§56/§58/§89 therefore encodes semantics from outside `specs/`. A decision is needed: either accept Annex D + brief obligation 5 and DS-v1 as the normative source for this formalization (and cite them), or add the contracts to `specs/`.
142	
143	**P1. Pool slot layout is under-determined, and the choice changes accepted programs.** D.1: "Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage`". `newPool(storage, internal)` receives no slot description. The draft picks the direct children (`newPoolEff` HP:116). Example: storage `S = {a: {x, y}, b}`. "Slots = children" gives 2 slots `a, b`, so a third `allocSlot` gives `fail`. "Slots = leaves" gives 3 slots `x, y, b`, so the third gives `ok`. A storage that is a single leaf gives 0 slots under the draft, so every `allocSlot` gives `fail`.
144	
145	**P2. Outcome of `freeSlot` on a free slot whose generation matches.** D.3: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" says it must not succeed, but not whether it gives `fail` or `reject`. Example (`pool_free_entry_handle` HZ:977): on a fresh pool, the fabricated handle `⟨0,0,0⟩` names free slot 0 of generation 0. The draft gives `ok`. The contract excludes `ok`, but `fail` (like `resolve`'s "slot … libre ⇒ fail") and `reject` are both possible readings.
146	
147	**P3. `resolve`: `reject` (no right) vs `fail` (bad handle) when both hold.** The right in D.2 ("exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis") includes the effective mode, which depends on the state. Spec v0 §77 orders the arena's analogous checks as availability `fail` (77.4) **before** the effective-right `reject` (77.5). Jalon3 H31a ("Deux `resolve Modify` simultanés, **quels que soient les handles** : le second `reject`") and the draft (HZ:590, `ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 1, 7⟩ .modify h31 .reject` with a stale generation 7) put `reject` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)` gives `reject` in the draft and `fail` under the §77 analogy. §58 defers to "the operation's contract", which does not settle it.
148	
149	**P4. Scope of "excluding `internal` and its ancestors" in `freeSlot`.**
150	- (a) D.3 lists only "aucune dépendance utilisable ne serait invalidée, aucune feuille n'est épinglée, et aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; the brief says "preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors". O12.3 includes "No place remaining usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, **its root**, …". Example: a pool whose `internal` is the storage root (the `pb` setup HZ:565). If some usable place carries `internal` in `D` through `depend` (O5), the literal O12.3 rejects `freeSlot` (draft `EndUseAnchorOK` MM03:3989, `¬ IsRootOf`), although `freeSlot` leaves `internal` active. Whether the exemption also covers O12.3's root clause is not stated.
151	- (b) Kernel side, for the kernel mapper: in O12.2, "No active descendant over the leaves of `place` … is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning", the descendant has no stated referent. The draft's literal reading (`EndUseAccessOK` MM03:3979: every active derived authority on an ending leaf) forbids `endUse` of any value stored inside an issued arena block while the block authority, held by the destination outside the block, is active. That authority is the one through which O12.1's `Modify` is exercised. Witness: `pool_freeSlot_derived_internal` HZ:925. It decides whether `freeSlot` can be a kernel `endUse` step (§2 item 8).
152	
153	**P5. D.3 contradicts itself when `dst` lies in the allocated slot.** "Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit` … l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot" holds only if `dst` lies outside the slot. Unlike O18.2 ("leaf `destination` is not in `region`"), `allocSlot` does not exclude it. Example: a frame with `Modify` on the pool value has `internal` exercisable (§43, holder chain), so it has `HasRight .modify q` for a free-slot leaf `q`. `allocSlot(pool, dst := q)` satisfies every D.3 precondition (usable leaf, not `Init`, no authority held), picks slot `q`, and writes the handle into it: the slot becomes `Init`.
154	
155	**P6. "Les entrées libres sont `Uninit`" (D.1) is not an invariant of the open model.** A frame with `Modify` on the pool value can `derive` from `internal` onto a free slot (O1) and `write3` it (O10). That is the same mechanism as the draft counterexample `pool_inv_not_preserved` HP:1830 (a derive from the companion onto a free entry). A later `allocSlot` then hands out an `Init` slot even if `newPool` required `Uninit` storage. D.4 assigns encapsulation to Spec 9. The property can be stated only as an `allocSlot`/`freeSlot` effect, not as a reachable-state theorem, unless Spec 9 encapsulation is modeled.
156	
157	**P7. DataStack "a cell above m" is undefined.** It could mean `[m.top, top)` (cells that `rewind` returns) or any index ≥ `m.top`. Example (draft `opsE8`, `case_rewind_reading` DSL:1013): after an intermediate `rewind`, an authority `9` derived from `internal` covers cell 3 above the current top. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is accepted by the draft; under the literal "covers a cell above m" it is rejected. Safety is the same either way, since the next `push` of cell 3 is rejected by the effective right (§43 case 3). A "region issued after m" reading (Derivability (f) 7) gives a third answer for grown blocks (`opsE4`).
158	
159	**P8. DataStack ordering of statics against `fail`.** §58 says statics come before dynamic availability "according to the operation's contract". DS-v1 (as quoted) does not order (i) `rewind`'s administrative right (§36) against the dead/foreign-mark `fail`, or (ii) `push`/`grow` statics against the no-room `fail`. §75 describes the derived issue as "split followed by store (after checking availability)", which suggests availability first. §77 puts statics first. Example: a callee with no right over the stack value (`opsZ` DSL:1029) calls `rewind` with a removed mark. The draft gives `fail`; statics first gives `reject`.
160	
161	**P9. DataStack `grow` details not covered by DS-v1 (as quoted):**
162	- `extra = 0`: the draft gives `reject` (DSL:221 `0 < extra`).
163	- whether `b` must be releasable (the draft checks `ReleasePre` statically);
164	- the destination after the block value has been transferred: the draft stores into the recorded `Blk.dst`, which may then be `Moved` and no longer the holder (Derivability (f)).
165	
166	**P10 (low). `resolveMany Observe` with invalid handles.** D.2 states the atomic `fail` ("toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**") only in the `Modify` sentence. For `Observe`, it says only "sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction". The natural reading (an invalid handle gives an atomic `fail`) is not written down.
167	
168	No contradiction with the Charter was found. Charter §4.1 lists the five guarantees and §3.4 sends features to libraries; both are consistent with every item above.
169	
170	---
171	
172	## 5. Representation choices recommended (they change no accepted program)
173	
174	- **R1.** One library record `Lib` (arenas, pools, stacks, `nextPool`, `nextMark`, ghost `res`) beside `S3`, with a single function `liveInternals : Lib → S3 → List AuthorityId` for §56. This follows §38 and §56 ("Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel").
175	- **R2.** Pool identity as a counter (`nId`), mark identity as a counter (`fresh`): §9 "A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation".
176	- **R3.** A stack's identity is its registry index; stacks are never removed, so indices are never reused. `Mark = (stack, id, top)` as in the draft.
177	- **R4.** Ghost resolution registry `Res` (companion, mode, entries tagged with slot and generation), read only by `unresolve` and by the invariants. It is auxiliary information that creates no rights (§38 last sentence, applied to library state).
178	- **R5.** `resolveMany Modify` realized as `derive` companion + `split` on the entry footprints. With the distinctness check placed first, this accepts exactly the batches that successive `derive`s from the companion would accept, because entries are disjoint (`pool_entries_disjoint`).
179	- **R6.** Library operations as relations with `ok | fail | reject` (`POutcome`/`Out`), `fail` carrying the unchanged state. `allocSlot` is a relation over any free slot. Executable runners (`pexec`, `drun`) keep a deterministic choice (`firstFree`) and are proven to agree with the relation on every result they return (DESIGN.md, Representation).
180	- **R7.** Stack availability as the index `top`, with `available st := st.cells.drop st.top`. This is equivalent to an explicit leaf set (§46 `available: Set<Leaf>`) because `push` and `grow` take cells only at the top and `rewind` returns exactly `[m.top, top)`. A lemma stating that equivalence makes C5 literal.
181	- **R8.** Handle as `(poolId, slot index, gen)` with the slot index read as a position in `Pool.slots`; a slot index out of range never names an entry (`fail`).
182	- **R9.** `AdminRight` (§2 item 3) shared by arenas, pools and stacks, so one definition carries the §36 citation.
183	
184	I did not check that any build compiles: no Lean was run. Line numbers come from `git show formal/derivability_0.1:<path>`. The DS-v1 rows rest only on the brief's quoted summary.

import Ern.Derived.Arena
import Ern.MM23

/-!
# DataStack, a library instance over the kernel (derivability pass 0.1, question 2)

A stack administers a storage through an authority `internal` held by the stack value, as an arena
does (candidate Spec 1 §36, §46), with library metadata: the ordered leaves of the storage, the
top, the issued blocks and the live marks. Its operations are built on kernel steps and on the
derived `issue` and `reset` of question 1 (`Ern.Derived.Arena`):

* `push`: the restricted `issue` at the top, its static clauses (§77.1, §77.2) checked before the
  room, realised by `split` of `internal` on the cells then `store` of the block into the
  destination; `fail` when no room is left;
* `mark`: a mark (stack, fresh identifier, top), metadata only;
* `rewind`: the derived `reset` on the cells above the mark, `split` of `internal` on them then
  `release` of the derived authority; `fail` for a mark that is not live in the stack;
* `grow`: in place, `release` of the last block, then the derived `issue` of a region of the same
  base and of larger size into the same destination, which is `Init`; `fail` when no room is left.

Every `ok` step of the library takes kernel steps of `Reachable` only (`dexec_reach`). The theorems
of the brief are `rewind_rejects_live_above`, `mark_no_aba` (with `rewind_removes`),
`rewind_keeps_older_marks`,
`grow_same_base`, `grow_keeps_prefix_init` and `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` (through the refinement
`Ern.MM23`, unchanged). The decisions the brief does not settle are listed in the report
(`formal/reports/Derivability_v0.1.md`, (c) and (f)).
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.DataStack

open Ern.MM03 Ern.HandlePool Ern.MM03.Horrors Ern.Derived.Arena

/-- A block issued by a stack: base and size in the cells of the stack, authority, destination. -/
structure Blk where
  base : Nat
  size : Nat
  auth : Nat
  dst : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A mark (brief: "(pile, identifiant frais, sommet)"). -/
structure Mark where
  stack : Nat
  id : Nat
  top : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- A stack (brief: "stockage, `internal`, sommet, liste ordonnée des marques vivantes"); `cells`
are the ordered leaves of the storage, its footprint at creation; `blocks` the issued blocks,
oldest first. The stack value is the holder of `internal`. -/
structure Stack where
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  cells : List Nat
  top : Nat
  blocks : List Blk
  marks : List Mark
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- State of the library: the kernel state, the stacks (the identity of a stack is its index) and
the next fresh mark identifier. -/
structure DS where
  s : S3
  stacks : List Stack
  fresh : Nat

/-- Outcome of a library operation; `fail` leaves the state unchanged (§58). -/
inductive Out where
  | ok (d : DS)
  | fail
  | reject

/-- The `n` cells of the stack from the index `b`. -/
def cellsOf (st : Stack) (b n : Nat) : List Nat := (st.cells.drop b).take n

/-- The cells above the mark `m`, from its top to the current top: those that `rewind m` returns
to the available part (brief: "les régions au-dessus de `m`"). A region issued after `m` and still
below the top lies there, but not every such region does: a block grown after `m` from a base below
`m` starts below it, and a region issued after `m` and returned by an intermediate `rewind` lies
above the current top (`case_rewind_reading`; report, (f)). -/
def above (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : List Nat := cellsOf st m.top (st.top - m.top)

/-- The stack seen as an administration of its storage, for `MetaRightM` and `blockOf`. -/
def Stack.arena (st : Stack) : Arena := ⟨st.storage, st.internal, [], []⟩

/-- No active authority is held by the destination (O8.2, §77.2). -/
def NoHeld (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True

instance (s : S3) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (NoHeld s dst) := by unfold NoHeld; infer_instance

/-- Static preconditions of `push` of the cells `r`, checked before the room (§58, §77.4), those of
the restricted `issue` (`IssueStaticR`, §77.1 and §77.2): the stack is live, the current frame has
exercisable `Modify` on the stack value (`MetaRightM`), and the destination is a usable leaf under
exercisable `Modify`, not `Init`, holding no active authority and outside `r`. The brief's "`fail`
si pas de place" stands for both the inclusion of the region in the storage (a static clause of
§77.2) and its availability (§77.4): `push` fails when the cells requested go past the storage. -/
def PushStatic (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRightM s st.arena ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ NoHeld s dst ∧ dst ∉ r

instance (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (PushStatic s st r dst) := by
  unfold PushStatic; infer_instance

/-- The derived `issue` (question 1, `issue_as_kernel_split`): `split` of `internal` on `r`, then
`store` of the block into `dst`. -/
def IssueSeq (k : K) (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  SplitPre k s st.internal [r] ∧ StorePre (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) s.A.length dst

instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (st : Stack)
    (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (IssueSeq k s st r dst) := by
  unfold IssueSeq; infer_instance

/-- Arrival state of the derived `issue`. -/
def issueSeqEff (s : S3) (st : Stack) (r : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 :=
  storeEff (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena r)) s.A.length dst

/-- The derived `reset` on the cells above `m` (question 1, `reset_as_kernel`): `split` of
`internal` on them, then `release` of the derived authority. -/
def RewindSeq (k : K) (s : S3) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) : Prop :=
  SplitPre k s st.internal [above st m] ∧
    ReleasePre (s.addAuth (blockOf s st.arena (above st m))) s.A.length

instance (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] (s : S3) (st : Stack) (m : Mark) :
    Decidable (RewindSeq k s st m) := by
  unfold RewindSeq; infer_instance

/-- The guard of §56 for `internal` `i`: no live arena and no live stack already uses it. -/
def Guard56 (d : DS) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ ar ∈ d.s.arenas, d.s.Active ar.internal → ar.internal ≠ i) ∧
    ∀ x ∈ d.stacks, d.s.Active x.internal → x.internal ≠ i

instance (d : DS) (i : Nat) : Decidable (Guard56 d i) := by unfold Guard56; infer_instance

section Ops
variable (k : K) [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]

/-- Creation of a stack on `storage` administered by `internal` (as O17, §76): the preconditions of
`newArena` and the guard of §56 on both registries, arenas and stacks. -/
def newStack (d : DS) (storage i : Nat) : Out :=
  if NewArenaPreNG d.s storage i ∧ Guard56 d i then
    .ok { d with stacks := d.stacks ++ [⟨storage, i, footprint d.s.P storage, 0, [], []⟩] }
  else .reject

/-- `push size dst` on the stack `j` (brief: "émission au sommet (`issue` restreint)"): the static
clauses of the restricted `issue` (`PushStatic`), then `fail` when fewer than `size` cells are left,
then the derived `issue` of the `size` cells at the top into `dst`. Its kernel part being the
derived `issue`, `push` also asks clause 5 of `store` (O8.5), which the restricted `issue` does not
(`issue_as_kernel_split`, for registered arenas). Its exact relation to `IssueR` is not proven here:
a stack is not an entry of the arena registry, and the room stands for availability. `size` may be
zero: the block then has an empty footprint, as the
restricted `issue` of the empty region (`ce_empty_region`), and it blocks no `rewind`. -/
def push (d : DS) (j size dst : Nat) : Out :=
  match d.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    if PushStatic d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
      if st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length then
        if IssueSeq k d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst then
          .ok { d with
            s := issueSeqEff d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst
            stacks := d.stacks.set j
              { st with
                top := st.top + size
                blocks := st.blocks ++ [⟨st.top, size, d.s.A.length, dst⟩] } }
        else .reject
      else .fail
    else .reject

/-- `mark` on the stack `j` (brief): `ok`, a mark (stack, fresh identifier, top) appended to the
live marks. -/
def mark (d : DS) (j : Nat) : Out :=
  match d.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st => .ok { d with
      stacks := d.stacks.set j { st with marks := st.marks ++ [⟨j, d.fresh, st.top⟩] }
      fresh := d.fresh + 1 }

/-- `rewind m` on the stack `j` (brief): `fail` when `m` is not a live mark of the stack; then the
derived `reset` on the cells above `m`, `split` of `internal` on them and `release`, which rejects
when an active authority derived from `internal` covers one of them (`rewind_rejects_live_above`)
and also when the current frame cannot exercise `internal` at `Modify` (O2.1, the restricted
`MetaRight` of §78.1); `ok`: the top returns to the top of `m`, the blocks whose base is above it
are forgotten, `m` and the later marks are removed, the older marks stay (`rewind_removes`). A stack
that does not exist rejects (no stack value). -/
def rewind (d : DS) (j : Nat) (m : Mark) : Out :=
  match d.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    if m ∈ st.marks then
      if RewindSeq k d.s st m then
        .ok { d with
          s := releaseEff (d.s.addAuth (blockOf d.s st.arena (above st m))) d.s.A.length
          stacks := d.stacks.set j
            { st with
              top := m.top
              blocks := st.blocks.filter (·.base < m.top)
              marks := st.marks.takeWhile (· ≠ m) } }
      else .reject
    else .fail

/-- `grow b extra` on the stack `j` (brief: in place only). Static clauses, checked before the room
(§58): `b` is the authority of the last block, at the top, `extra` is positive ("taille plus
grande"), `b` can be released, the stack is live, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` on
the stack value (`MetaRightM`), and the destination recorded for the block is outside the new region
(§77.2, "vérifiée avant le `fail` de disponibilité"). `fail` when fewer than `extra` cells follow
the block; otherwise `release` of `b`, then the derived `issue` of the region of the same base and of
size `size + extra` into that destination. The other clauses on the destination concern the state
after the release and are those of `store`. The destination is `Init` (the first `store` wrote it)
unless the block value was moved out of it (`Moved`): the derived `issue` accepts both (O8.2), the
restricted `issue` rejects the `Init` case (§77.2, report (c)). -/
def grow (d : DS) (j b extra : Nat) : Out :=
  match d.stacks[j]? with
  | none => .reject
  | some st =>
    match st.blocks.getLast? with
    | none => .reject
    | some x =>
      if 0 < extra ∧ x.auth = b ∧ x.base + x.size = st.top ∧ ReleasePre d.s b ∧
          d.s.Active st.internal ∧ MetaRightM d.s st.arena ∧
          x.dst ∉ cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra) then
        if x.base + x.size + extra ≤ st.cells.length then
          if IssueSeq k (releaseEff d.s b) st (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst then
            .ok { d with
              s := issueSeqEff (releaseEff d.s b) st (cellsOf st x.base (x.size + extra)) x.dst
              stacks := d.stacks.set j
                { st with
                  top := x.base + x.size + extra
                  blocks := st.blocks.dropLast ++ [⟨x.base, x.size + extra, d.s.A.length, x.dst⟩] } }
          else .reject
        else .fail
      else .reject

/-- Operations of a run of the library: a kernel or arena step, or a stack operation. -/
inductive DOp where
  | kernel (o : Op)
  | newStack (storage i : Nat)
  | push (j size dst : Nat)
  | mark (j : Nat)
  | rewind (j : Nat) (m : Mark)
  | grow (j b extra : Nat)

/-- The guard of §56 that a kernel `newArena` adds in the library: the registry of the stacks. -/
def KGuard (d : DS) : Op → Prop
  | .newArena _ i => ∀ x ∈ d.stacks, d.s.Active x.internal → x.internal ≠ i
  | _ => True

instance (d : DS) (o : Op) : Decidable (KGuard d o) := by
  cases o <;> unfold KGuard <;> infer_instance

/-- A step of the library. A kernel `newArena` also consults the registry of the stacks (§56). -/
def dexec (d : DS) : DOp → Out
  | .kernel o =>
    if KGuard d o then
      match kexec k d.s o with
      | some s' => .ok { d with s := s' }
      | none => .reject
    else .reject
  | .newStack st i => DataStack.newStack d st i
  | .push j size dst => DataStack.push k d j size dst
  | .mark j => DataStack.mark d j
  | .rewind j m => DataStack.rewind k d j m
  | .grow j b extra => DataStack.grow k d j b extra

/-- A run of the library: `some` of the final state when every step is `ok`. -/
def drun (d : DS) : List DOp → Option DS
  | [] => some d
  | o :: os =>
    match dexec k d o with
    | .ok d' => drun d' os
    | _ => none

end Ops

/-- The initial state of the library. -/
def DS.init : DS := ⟨S3.init [], [], 0⟩

/-! ## Inversion of the `ok` steps -/

section Inv
variable {k : K} [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')]

theorem newStack_ok {d d' : DS} {st i : Nat} (h : newStack d st i = .ok d') :
    NewArenaPreNG d.s st i ∧ Guard56 d i ∧
      d' = { d with stacks := d.stacks ++ [⟨st, i, footprint d.s.P st, 0, [], []⟩] } := by
  unfold newStack at h

  · rename_i hp; cases h; exact ⟨hp.1, hp.2, rfl⟩
  · cases h

theorem push_ok {d d' : DS} {j size dst : Nat} (h : push k d j size dst = .ok d') :
    ∃ st, d.stacks[j]? = some st ∧ PushStatic d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst ∧
      st.top + size ≤ st.cells.length ∧
      IssueSeq k d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst ∧
      d' = { d with
        s := issueSeqEff d.s st (cellsOf st st.top size) dst
        stacks := d.stacks.set j
          { st with
